title: Extend the rack's anti-tip foot before drawing a server out to service
instruction: The grey server needs to come out of the rack to its service position. First pull the yellow stabiliser foot out of the bottom of the rack, about 8 cm, along the floor. Only then draw the server straight out on its steel rails, about 10 cm, toward you. Slide both along the table without lifting them, and do not move the server before the foot is out.
context: Rack and server installation guides warn that extending equipment from a rack whose stabiliser or anti-tip feet are not deployed can tip the rack onto the technician; the feet are pulled out first, and only then is a server drawn out on its slide rails to the service position. Both moves are slides, not lifts. The order is the skill: the end state alone does not show it, so it is checked every step. Unlike TK-QGZWGP (unload a cantilevered plank without letting it tip), where tipping is avoided by the order of unloading, here a separate stabiliser must be deployed before a part may move; unlike the chest tip-restraint task (bolt a chest to the wall, then load a drawer), the load is a server drawn out on its rails; and DataCenterBench has no rack-safety or rail task. Done by: data-center and computer equipment repairers, telecommunications equipment installers (O*NET 49-2011.00, 49-2022.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Rack front: three fixed dark uprights 2 x 2 x 15 cm at x 46, y 15, 31.5 and 44.5. Slide rails: two fixed steel bars 28 x 0.8 x 1.5 cm along x, centred at x 36 and y 26.7 and 17.3. Server: a loose grey box 16 cm deep (x) by 8 cm wide by 4.5 cm tall, 350 g, on the table between the rails centred at x 42, y 22. Foot guide: two fixed dark walls 12 x 0.5 x 1 cm along x from x 40, centred at y 40.05 and 35.95. Stabiliser foot: a loose yellow bar 14 cm long (x), 3 cm wide, 2 cm tall, 150 g, in the guide centred at x 43, y 38, its pull end 4 cm in front of the rack.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses, with the grippers open at the end. 0.25 for the stabiliser foot extended: drawn out 7 to 11 cm, still in its guide, square within 10 degrees, flat on the table. 0.5 once the server has also been drawn out at least 5 cm. 1.0 with the foot extended and the server at its service position: 10 cm out within 1.5 cm, within 5 mm of its rails' centre line, square within 5 degrees, flat on the table, still. Tip hazard: if the server's centre ever moves more than 1 cm from its start while the foot is not extended, the score is 0 for the rest of the trial. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: score 1, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Push the server back into the rack and the foot back into its guide, both to their marks; the uprights, rails and guide do not move. On a real rig the order is judged from the trial video.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The rack lies on the table: the server slides on the table between its rails rather than on telescopic slides, the foot slides in an open guide with no end stop or latch, and the rack is fixed, so tipping is not simulated: it is judged from the order of the two slides, every step. The server is a scaled short-depth box.
